text:
jordan.sales: HS Bank wants Private deployment in their AWS VPC. They need to preserve original client source IP for downstream logging/IDS. Preference is PrivateLink (endpoint service) over VPC peering. Also asked about minimal firewall rules and any cost delta for PrivateLink vs peering. Need a NetOps-ready checklist to hand to their infra team. Can someone own a short runbook?

maria.se: Clarifying q: do they insist on preserving original source IP all the way to their app servers, or just want it in our logs? There are 3 common patterns:
1) PrivateLink (endpoint service + NLB) — traffic comes from customer ENIs to our NLB. Preserving the client IP to backend requires special NLB/target config or using Proxy Protocol / x-forwarded-for. We can also terminate TLS at the NLB and forward client IP in headers.
2) VPC Peering / Transit — keeps full L3 visibility; source IP preserved end-to-end but requires peering across accounts and route management.
3) Reverse proxy inside customer's VPC (SNI-proxy or our sidecar) — preserves source but introduces extra hop.
I'll outline tradeoffs and a recommended pattern depending on their security requirements.

sam.netops: From NetOps point:
- Minimal firewall: allow outbound TCP 443 from customer subnets to the PrivateLink endpoint (or to our public egress IPs if using a proxy). No inbound open ports required on customer's side for PrivateLink.
- If they want to preserve source IP to backends and we use Proxy Protocol, we'll ask them to allow the NLB healthcheck + NLB IP range in SGs.
- If they insist on NAT + static egress EIP: they can NAT traffic through an edge appliance and we can whitelist those EIPs on our side.

Example security group / firewall snippet (customer side):
```
# Allow app hosts to reach Redwood PrivateLink endpoint
ALLOW TCP 443 from 10.1.0.0/20 to vpce-xxxxxxx
# If using egress NAT, allow return ports
ALLOW TCP/UDP ephemeral 1024-65535 from 0.0.0.0/0 established
```

And our ask list for them:
- Provide expected peak TPS and GB/day
- Desired source-ip preservation level (logs only / all way to app)
- Approved NAT egress IPs if they require static outbound
- Will they accept Proxy Protocol / x-forwarded-for headers?

elaine.se: Pricing note for sales: PrivateLink typically adds per-GB data processing + NLB costs vs peering where you pay standard VPC egress in their cloud. Also operational uplift: PrivateLink is easier for multi-account access control, peering is cheaper at high-volume but needs route management. I'll add a short cost delta estimate once we have GB/mo.

jordan.sales: Perfect. Can we turn the NetOps ask list into a 1-page handoff to send to the customer today? Need it to include exact ports and the text they can drop into their firewall request ticket.

sam.netops: I'll own the handoff. Draft below — feel free to copy/paste when you send.

```
Subject: Redwood Private Deployment — Network Handoff

1) Connectivity option: AWS PrivateLink (recommended) OR VPC Peering (if strict source IP preservation required)
2) Firewall rules (customer-managed):
   - Allow outbound TCP 443 from app subnets to the VPCE endpoint ID (will provide IPs once VPCE created)
   - Allow inbound healthcheck from NLB (if using Proxy Protocol)
   - If using static NAT egress, allow our documented egress EIPs (we'll supply)
3) Required info to provide back to Redwood:
   - VPCE ID / subnet mapping or peering/aws-account-id
   - Expected peak requests per second and GB/month
   - Whether Proxy Protocol / x-forwarded-for is acceptable
4) Timeline & contacts:
   - NetOps: sam.netops@redwood.com
   - SE: maria.se@redwood.com
```

infra-deploy-bot: Ticket created: RDW-5381 assigned to @sam.netops — onboarding runbook task created :white_check_mark:

maria.se: I'll update the customer email with this handoff and schedule a short call to confirm the VPCE details. @jordan.sales I'll include cost note from @elaine.se once you share the usage numbers.

jordan.sales: Thanks all — sending in 30m.
